title: fix(plugin-sharing): two sharing rules that reach one user on one record keep one grant each, so the widest level wins
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbFwjhzyd3V4iJP6ii9CN5kG)_

Fixes #33683

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:两条共享规则在同一条记录上命中同一个用户时,各自保留一行 `sys_record_share`(按规则 id 区分),不再互相覆盖;用户最终拿到其中最高的权限。
- **为什么改**:原来第二条规则会覆盖第一条规则的那一行,最后写入的规则说了算。HotCRM 的项目经理同时是项目成员,"成员只读"覆盖了"经理可编辑",经理打不开编辑、也无法配置项目成员(hotcrm#2316,18.5.0 发版阻塞)。撤销其中一条规则时还会误删另一条规则仍然给的权限。
- **风险与回滚**:只改 `SharingService.grant` 查找已有行的条件(规则授权多带一个 `source_id`);读写闸门本来就按多行取最宽,不用改。手工共享照旧一人一行。无迁移、无索引变更;历史上被合并的行会在该规则下次对账(启动回填或记录写入)时自动拆开。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts` 的 `grant` 查找条件那一段;`src/field-recipient.test.ts` 末尾新增的 describe;`src/record-share-organization-stamp.test.ts` 改动的那条钉子(跨组织 404 的剩余入口)。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing exec vitest run src/field-recipient.test.ts -t 'two rules reaching'`,预期 11 条全绿;把 `grant` 里的 `source_id` 那一行删掉再跑,预期 11 条全红。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`SharingService.grant` looked up an existing share row by `(object_name, record_id, recipient_type, recipient_id, source)` and, when it found one, overwrote its `access_level` and `source_id`. Every sharing rule grants through it with `source: 'rule'` and `sourceId: rule.id`, so two rules that reach one user on one record shared one row and the last rule written won, whatever its level. Each rule's reconcile and revoke read by its own `source_id`, so the merged row belonged to whichever rule wrote last: revoking that rule removed access the other rule still granted, revoking the other rule removed nothing, and every whole-rule pass of the other rule wrote the row back to its own level (access flapping between passes).

A grant from the rule evaluator's system path (a system context, any `source` other than `manual`, a `sourceId`) is now looked up by that id too, so there is one row per rule and recipient. The read side needs no change: `buildReadFilter` collects the record ids of every row the user holds, and `checkEdit` / `buildWriteFilter` ask for any row with a write level, so the effective access is already the highest level across rows, as the `grant` jsdoc said for manual and rule rows side by side. Only that path supplies a `source_id` that names a rule. A manual grant, and any grant made outside the rule evaluator's system path, keeps the four-part key, so a repeated direct grant still upserts its one row.

This follows the triage ruling (comment 6890597594, "Merge to the highest access per (record, principal) and pin both write orders."): the merge is the read gates' maximum across rows; each rule keeps the row only it reconciles. The other shape (one row, level recomputed from every rule still reaching the user on each grant and revoke) was weighed on the four axes and not taken:

- **Business need**: both shapes deliver the HotCRM case (`project_team_read` + `project_manager_edit` on `crm_project`); the per-rule row also covers every other overlap (two position rules, a position and a field rule) with no extra work.
- **Long-term soundness**: per-rule rows keep the existing invariant that a rule reconciles and revokes only what its own `source_id` names (`ruleGrantScope`), which every revoke path already relies on (`revokeRuleGrants`, `reconcileRuleForUser`, `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients`, the declared-rule activation purge). One recomputed row would make every one of those paths ask every other rule whether it still reaches the user on that record, a criteria read and a recipient expansion per rule per revoke.
- **Hard for AI to get wrong**: one row per rule is the shape the reconcile already assumes; a recomputed row needs every future revoke path to remember the cross-rule recompute, the kind of omission that caused this defect.
- **Startup focus**: a three-line key change, no schema, index or migration (`sys_record_share` has no unique index; its indexes are `(object_name, recipient_type, recipient_id)`, `(object_name, record_id)` and `(source, source_id)`).

Existing data: a row two rules already share carries the last writer's `source_id`. The other rule's next reconcile (the boot backfill, a write to the record, a whole-rule pass) finds no row of its own and writes one, so the user regains its access with no migration. Pinned below.

## Tests

New pins, in `src/field-recipient.test.ts` as one top-level describe (the harness that already drives field and position rules and the real gates):

- both write orders (read rule then edit rule, edit rule then read rule) on the per-record pass: two rows, `checkEdit` answers `allow`, a team member who is not the manager answers `deny`;
- both orders on the whole-rule pass, then the read rule's pass again: the edit grant is not lowered;
- both orders, then revoke the edit rule: the read row stays and the record stays in the read filter, `checkEdit` answers `deny`;
- both orders, then revoke the read rule: the edit row stays, `checkEdit` answers `allow`;
- a position edit rule beside a field read rule, both orders; the user leaves the position and the membership pass (`reconcileRuleForUser`) revokes that rule's row only, the read stays;
- a legacy merged row is split by the next per-record pass.

Three direct pins in `src/sharing-service.test.ts`: a second rule's grant writes its own row and leaves the first rule's row and level alone, and the same rule granting again upserts its own row; a manual grant keeps one row per recipient whatever `sourceId` the caller sends; a direct (non-system) grant with a non-manual `source` and two different `sourceId`s keeps one row.

Two existing pins held the merged row and are updated:

- `src/sharing-rule.test.ts` (#8710 ledger-read cache): "One share row, not two" now expects one row per rule (`['u_cfo', 'u_cfo']`); the pin's subject, one ledger read per pass, is unchanged.
- `src/record-share-organization-stamp.test.ts` (#14484, the loud `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` on an update the wall cannot reach): the pin reached the 404 through a grant from a DIFFERENT rule, which no longer finds the other organization's row. The remaining road in is a grant of the SAME rule id from another organization (a declared rule served under a wall is one projection per organization, all carrying the rule's name as `source_id`), so the pin now uses one rule id for both rows, and the comment says so. The measured shape it holds (throw 404, the stored row keeps its stamp, level and source) is unchanged.

<details><summary>Runs (fix at 95c02cdd; suites re-read after the main merge at 5b7a3935 where noted)</summary>

- `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` full suite at 95c02cdd: Test Files 74 passed (74), Tests 1524 passed (1524). The four touched test files again after the edits: 3 files 232 passed, `sharing-service.test.ts` 155 passed.
- Dependents (direction: consumers of plugin-sharing, built from the merged tree 5b7a3935): `@objectstack/plugin-security` Test Files 267 passed, Tests 6681 passed and 45 skipped; `@objectstack/service-automation` Test Files 282 passed, Tests 3976 passed. `runtime`, `cli`, `verify`, `qa/scenarios` and `qa/dogfood` are declared to CI: no exported signature or wire shape moves.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing typecheck` exit 0 (tsc, scripts tsconfig, test-layer check: 3 pinned signatures held, unchanged). `pnpm lint` exit 0.

**Ablation 1**, the `source_id` key spread deleted from `grant` (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 to 0, blob beeff2f5 to 7290dfd7): all 11 new describe pins red, for example `per-record pass, edit rule first, then read`: `expected [ 'srule_team_read:read' ] to deeply equal [ 'srule_manager_edit:edit', 'srule_team_read:read' ]`, the card's repro. The direct `sharing-service.test.ts` pin red too: `expected 'shr_rule' not to be 'shr_rule'`. Restored: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

**Ablation 3** (review fix, head b1aed3bb), the system-path guard dropped (`context?.isSystem &&` removed): `a direct (non-system) grant keeps one row per recipient whatever non-manual source and sourceId it sends` red, `expected 2 to be 1`; the two system-path pins stay green. Restored: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty. plugin-sharing full suite at b1aed3bb: 74/74 files, 1525/1525 tests; typecheck 0, `pnpm lint` 0.

**Ablation 2**, the manual exclusion dropped (`source !== 'manual' &&` removed): `a manual grant keeps one row per recipient whatever sourceId the caller sends` red, `expected 2 to be 1`. Restored: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The read gates read at most 5000 of a user's share rows per object (`buildReadFilter`, `buildWriteFilter`, `limit: 5000`). Rows beyond the cap are dropped silently, before and after this change; with one row per rule, a user two rules reach on N records now holds 2N rows, so the cap is met sooner. No real deployment is measured near it. Noted for the lane, not changed here.
